title: Comparison of chart sections with the terminal inverse-image unit
statement: Let $p:X\to S$ be a scheme morphism, $\Lambda$ a commutative ring, $G$ a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale site of $S$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], and $V\to S$, $W\to X$ etale objects. Let $\varphi:W\to V\times_S X$ be a morphism over $X$, and let $q:W\to V$ be its composite with the first projection [def-pc-fibre-product]. The map $G(V)\to (p^*G)(W)$ given by the inverse-image adjunction unit and restriction along $\varphi$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] is isomorphic as an arrow of $\Lambda$-modules to the terminal-object unit map $\Gamma(V,r^*G)\to\Gamma(V,q_*q^*r^*G)$, where $r:V\to S$. No flatness, quasi-compactness, or connectedness assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0EZX, first displayed formula and footnote 1; Tag 0A3H applied after restriction. Source APIs: Etale.upperStarIsoLocalizationRestriction and upperStarComp.

proof.text: Put j=W.hom and r=V.hom. The equation defining the chart gives j followed by p equal to q followed by r. Both j and r are etale.

The etale localization comparison identifies G(V) with terminal sections of r^*G, and sections of p^*G on W with terminal sections of j^*p^*G. Inverse-image composition identifies j^*p^*G with q^*r^*G using the equation of Step 1. These comparisons are isomorphisms.
The pullback of the terminal V-object along q is canonically the terminal W-object. Transport target sections along that isomorphism.

The unit equation for composite adjunctions and the restriction-unit equation identify the chart restriction of the unit for p with the terminal unit for q. The source and target comparisons therefore form a commutative square; Arrow.isoMk supplies the claimed arrow isomorphism.
